faq.a1: CaseroOk is a platform where tenants anonymously share their experiences with landlords to help others make informed decisions.

privacyPolicy.seoDescription: How we process your personal data at CaseroOk.
privacyPolicy.title: Privacy policy
privacyPolicy.section2Lead1Strong: Data provided by users who post reviews:
privacyPolicy.section2Lead1: review text, rating, and minimum anti-spam technical metadata (e.g., IP/UA).
privacyPolicy.section2Lead2Strong: Landlord/manager identifiers to deduplicate and group reviews:
privacyPolicy.section2Bullet1: We do not store personal data in plain text (name, phone, email).
privacyPolicy.section2Bullet2: We store only an irreversible hash (e.g., SHA-256) of normalized data (e.g., normalized phone or email).
privacyPolicy.section2Bullet3: The hash is computed on your device (frontend or extension) and only the hash is sent, never the original value.
privacyPolicy.section2Lead3: page views and events, without identifying you.
privacyPolicy.section3Body1: Voluntary user submission when posting a review.
privacyPolicy.section3Body2: Browser extension (Chrome/Firefox): only captures information visible on pages such as Idealista; computes the hash locally and queries the backend with that hash. It does not perform mass scraping or download personal data in plain text.
privacyPolicy.section4Bullet2: Group reviews by landlord/manager using hashes to avoid duplicates and improve search.
privacyPolicy.section4Bullet3: Abuse and spam prevention (rate limiting, technical signals).
privacyPolicy.section5Body1: Consent of the user submitting the review.
privacyPolicy.section5Body2: Legitimate interest (GDPR art. 6.1.f) for moderation, security, hash-based deduplication, and proper service operation. No automated decisions with legal effects are used.
privacyPolicy.section6Body: We do not share data with third parties except when legally required. We use infrastructure providers acting as processors (e.g., Supabase, {{hostingProvider}}), under GDPR-compliant contracts. International transfers may occur; in that case we apply appropriate safeguards (EU Standard Contractual Clauses).
privacyPolicy.section7Bullet1: Reviews and hashes: while the service is active or until you request deletion/blocking.
privacyPolicy.section8Body: You can request access, rectification, deletion, objection, restriction, and portability by writing to {{contactEmail}}. Note on hashes: since we do not store the original value, deletion is performed by blocking or deleting the associated hash. If you are an affected third party (e.g., landlord) and believe indirect identification exists, contact us to block the hash and de-index grouping.
privacyPolicy.section9Body: The service is not intended for minors under 14 years old. Submissions from minors are not accepted.
privacyPolicy.section10Body: We may update this policy. We will publish the current version with its update date.

cookiesPolicy.seoDescription: Information about cookie usage at CaseroOk.
cookiesPolicy.title: Cookies policy
cookiesPolicy.section1Bullet1: essential for the website to work (session, security, basic preferences).
cookiesPolicy.section1Bullet2: we count visits and site usage in aggregate, without storing cookies or identifiers in your browser.
cookiesPolicy.section1Body: We do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.
cookiesPolicy.section2Title: Why is there no cookie banner?
cookiesPolicy.section2Prefix: Because we only store what is technically essential in your browser, such as keeping you signed in, which does not require consent.
cookiesPolicy.section3Title: How to manage cookies in your browser
cookiesPolicy.section3Body: You can allow, block, or delete cookies from your browser settings.
cookiesPolicy.section4Body: To measure usage in aggregate and without cookies we use {{analyticsProvider}}.

termsOfUse.title: Terms of use
termsOfUse.section1Body: Regulate access to and use of {{projectName}}, a platform/blog for anonymous reviews about rental experiences.
termsOfUse.section2Body: The user is responsible for the truthfulness of what they publish and for complying with these rules.
termsOfUse.section3Bullet1: It is strictly forbidden to publish in free text personal data of third parties in plain text (full name, phone, email, exact address, or other identifiers).
termsOfUse.section3Bullet2: Insulting or defamatory language, hate speech, or incitement to violence.
termsOfUse.section3Bullet3: False information or content that infringes third-party rights.
termsOfUse.section4Body1: To group reviews of the same landlord/manager and avoid duplicates, the system may ask users to enter a landlord phone or email only in designated fields.
termsOfUse.section4Body2: That value is NEVER sent in plain text: it is normalized and hashed locally (e.g., SHA-256), and only the hash is sent.
termsOfUse.section4Body3: Publishing those values in review text or other visible fields is prohibited.
termsOfUse.section4Body4: The user agrees not to attempt re-identification or use hashes for purposes other than consultation within the service.
termsOfUse.section5Bullet1: Only processes information visible on sites such as Idealista.
termsOfUse.section5Bullet2: Computes a local hash and queries the backend with that hash to show whether related reviews exist.
termsOfUse.section5Bullet3: Does not download or store personal data in plain text.
termsOfUse.section6Body: We may moderate, hide, or remove content that breaches these conditions or the law. You can contact {{contactEmail}} to report abuse or request review.
termsOfUse.section7Body: Reviews are the responsibility of their authors. {{projectName}} does not guarantee accuracy and assumes no liability for decisions made based on reviews.
termsOfUse.section8Body: The user guarantees they have rights to publish their content and grants {{projectName}} a non-exclusive, free license to host and display it.
termsOfUse.section9Body: We may suspend accounts or publications for serious or repeated breaches.
termsOfUse.section10Body: Spanish law; jurisdiction of {{jurisdictionCity}}, unless mandatory law provides otherwise.

goodPractices.title: Best practices protocol
goodPractices.introTitle: To keep a useful and respectful space:
goodPractices.yesBullet1: Describe specific facts from your experience as a tenant.
goodPractices.yesBullet2: Be honest, respectful, and specific (approximate dates, objective incidents).
goodPractices.yesBullet3Intro: If you add a landlord phone/email in designated fields, keep in mind that:
goodPractices.yesBullet3a: It is normalized and hashed (e.g., SHA-256) on your device.
goodPractices.yesBullet3b: The original value is never stored.
goodPractices.yesBullet3c: The hash is only used to group reviews and match with platforms such as Idealista through the browser extension.
goodPractices.noBullet1: Include plain personal data in the review text.
goodPractices.noBullet2: Insults, disqualifications, rumors, or baseless accusations.
goodPractices.reportBody: If you find content that violates these rules, write to {{contactEmail}} including the URL and reason. We prioritize those reports.

dataNote.title: Where this data comes from
dataNote.official: The figures on this page are public, official data. Official data arrives late: the Ministry's reference rent goes up to 2024.
dataNote.more: How we work with the data
dataNote.reviewsTitle: Your review is the most up-to-date data
dataNote.reviewsText: What tenants say is the only thing that is current. The more reviews there are, with rent and size, the better we know what is happening on each street today, not two years ago.

reviews.name: Tenant reviews on CaseroOk
reviews.what: What people who rented say: landlord, home, deposit, rent paid and size. Every review is checked by hand before it is published and we never show names or emails.
reviews.limits: There are still few. It is the only source that covers what happens today on any street, so every review counts.

serpavi.name: Reference rent (SERPAVI)
serpavi.what: The Ministry of Housing computes rent per m² from contracts declared to the tax office, by census section, district and municipality, with history since 2011.
serpavi.limits: It lags a year and a half, mixes new and old contracts, and where there are few contracts the figure is only a guide. Individual contracts are not published.

deposits.name: Rental deposits lodged
deposits.what: The Generalitat Valenciana publishes every deposit lodged with its postcode (since 2020) and INCASÒL publishes the average rent of new contracts in Catalonia (since 2007). It is the closest thing to knowing what is signed today.
deposits.limits: Only available in those two regions. A deposit equals one month's rent; the current year is incomplete.

sales.name: Home sales and appraised value
sales.what: The Ministry of Housing publishes how many homes are sold in each municipality and their appraised value per m².
sales.limits: Appraised value only exists for municipalities over 25,000 inhabitants.

ipva.name: Rental price index (INE)
ipva.what: Yearly change in rent per municipality, computed by INE from tax data.
ipva.limits: It measures change, not prices, and has the same lag as SERPAVI.

catastro.name: Catastro
catastro.what: Year built, number of homes, floor area and use of each building, looked up live from the Dirección General del Catastro.
catastro.limits: It describes the building, not its condition or upkeep.

tensioned.name: Stressed rental markets
tensioned.what: Municipalities declared stressed markets under Ley 12/2023, with the rent limits that come with it.
tensioned.limits: The list changes with each resolution; we update it every quarter.

rentUpdate.seoTitle: How much can my rent go up? Spain 2026 calculator | CaseroOk
rentUpdate.seoDescription: Work out the legal maximum for your yearly rent update in Spain with the INE IRAV index and the 2 % cap until 2027.
rentUpdate.title: How much can your rent go up?
rentUpdate.intro: Enter your contract dates and what you pay. We show the highest update the law allows and whether what you are asked goes over it.
rentUpdate.pendingDecree: The 2 % cap comes from Real Decreto-ley 29/2026, in force since 8 October 2026. Congress has to validate it in early November; if it is rejected, we will update the calculator that day.

form.clause: Does your contract say the rent is updated every year?
form.clauseHint: Look for the rent or update clause: it usually mentions the IPC, the IRAV or a yearly update.
form.updateHint: The day the contract turns another year. We fill in the next anniversary.
form.rent: What you pay now per month
form.askedHint: The new monthly rent your landlord told you.
form.tensioned: Is the flat in a stressed rental market?
form.tensionedHint: How to know if your area is a stressed market

result.increase: Your rent can go up by {{amount}} a month at most ({{pct}}).
result.over: You are asked {{amount}} a month more than the law allows.
result.ok: What you are asked is within the legal limit.

why.irav: It is the IRAV for {{month}} ({{irav}}), the latest the INE had published on the update date. The law does not let the yearly update exceed it.
why.extraordinary: Until 31 December 2027, unless you sign a new agreement, the update cannot exceed 2 %, even though the IRAV for {{month}} is {{irav}}.

result.agreement: If you accept a different update in writing, the agreement applies, but never above the IRAV. Nobody can make you sign it.
result.estimated: The IRAV for your month is not published yet, so we use the latest one. Check again when the date comes.
result.tensioned: In a stressed market: if your rent is already above the Ministry reference index for your flat, updates until the end of 2027 cannot raise it at all. Check it by searching your address on CaseroOk.
result.rdl8: From 22 March to 29 April 2026 a 2 % cap was in force (Real Decreto-ley 8/2026) that Congress did not validate. If your update was notified in those dates, ask a tenants' union or the OMIC.
result.whatToDo: What to do: reply in writing with this calculation, ask for the INE certificate and keep paying the undisputed rent. If the landlord insists, ask a tenants' union or the OMIC.

noClause.title: Your rent cannot go up
noClause.text: If the contract has no update clause, the rent stays the same for as long as it lasts (article 18.1 of the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos).

beforeFirstYear.title: No update yet
beforeFirstYear.text: Rent can only be updated when the contract turns each year. Check the update date.

tooOld.title: Date outside the calculator
tooOld.text: We calculate updates from January 2025. For earlier dates, see the guide on the yearly rent update.

contractOnly.title: Your contract decides
contractOnly.text: Your contract predates 26 May 2023 and the update falls before 8 October 2026, so the clause index applies (usually the IPC) without the IRAV cap. Updates from 8 October 2026 do have that cap.

share.title: What do you pay? Help your neighbourhood
share.text: Official rent data arrives years late. If you share anonymously what you pay and how much it went up, people looking for a flat in your area will know the real price. It takes a couple of minutes.

rentUpdate.disclaimer: General information, not legal advice. For your own case, ask a tenants' union, the OMIC or a lawyer.
